'''Trandoshans''', also called '''T'doshok''', were large, bipedal [[Reptile|reptilian]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[humanoid]]s from the [[planet]] [[Trandosha]], and were renowned as great hunters. Trandoshans relished the thrill of a hunt, and were known to embark on a hunting related rite of passage. They were also famous for their ability to regenerate limbs and heal effectively. [[Garnac]] was a Trandoshan hunter who operated a game preserve on the [[moon]] [[Wasskah]], and oversaw his [[Dar|son's]] fatally failed rite of passage, which was done in the form of hunting a [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]]. One of the most feared [[bounty hunter]]s in [[the galaxy]] was a Trandoshan known as [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], who pulled jobs for various organizations, including the [[Galactic Empire]]. Other notable Trandoshans included the [[Jedi Master]] [[Sskeer]] and the information broker and cantina owner [[Ciddarin Scaleback]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Judging by the skull shape and number of teeth, these appear to be Trandoshans. They are fierce warriors and are tough to kill.|[[K-2SO]]|<ref name="Mighty Chewbacca">''[[The Mighty Chewbacca in the Forest of Fear!]]''</ref>}}
[[File:GinoleAssessingSskeer-2021THR10.png|thumb|left|300px|The skeleton of a Trandoshan, seen representing Jedi Master Sskeer.]]
Trandoshans were [[Sentience|sentient]] [[humanoid]]s with smooth, scaly skin. Trandoshans ranged from being tall and fairly gaunt, to being short and more rotund. Trandoshans were powerful beings, and had long thin arms that ended in either three thick digits, or four thin digits, including a thumb. Trandoshans had a pair of [[eye]]s set back on a pointed [[Bone|skull]], and a jaw filled with pointed [[Tooth|teeth]].<ref name="trando" /> Some Trandoshans even had a crown of feathers atop their skulls.<ref name="Chewbacca Returns Featurette">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Three|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Three]]</ref> They hatched from [[egg]]s, with individuals who shared a hatch of eggs calling each other [[clutchmate]]s.<ref name="Guardians of the Whills">[[Guardians of the Whills (novel)|''Guardians of the Whills'']]</ref> Trandoshans used their sharp claws to climb tall [[tree]]s in the [[forest]] or [[jungle]]s they naturally inhabited.<ref name="VE" />

The base urges of a Trandoshan [[brain]] included rage, fury, and aggression, but a Trandoshan could rise above those tendencies. However, the rare [[Magrak Syndrome]] would bring them back out over time.<ref name="The High Republic 12">[[The High Republic (2021) 12|''The High Republic'' (2021) 12]]</ref> Trandoshans often walked barefooted, and had feet with three digits each. A Trandoshan's skin [[color]] could vary wildly, and Trandoshans could be found with green, red, orange, brown, or yellow skin. Some Trandoshans, such as one named [[Smug]], had brownish-orange skin with red stripes on his face.<ref name="WookHunt">{{TCW|Wookiee Hunt}}</ref> They were able to regrow their limbs if they were severed<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref> and regrow lost scales. However, a [[plasma]] blast could prove so damaging that a Trandoshan's scales were never able to regrow.<ref name="Tempest Runner script">[[The High Republic: Tempest Runner (script)|''The High Republic: Tempest Runner'' script]]</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|The sun has risen. Let the hunt begin.|Garnac prepares for a hunt|<ref name="PadLost" />}}
Trandoshans came from the [[planet]] [[Trandosha]]<ref name="trando" /> in the [[Kashyyyk system]] of the [[Mid Rim Territories]] [[Mytaranor sector]].<ref name="Trandosha location">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' states that the [[moon]] [[Wasskah]] [[orbit]]s Trandosha. ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' further establishes Wasskah to be located in the [[Kashyyyk system]] of the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim's]] [[Mytaranor sector]], thereby providing a location for Trandosha.</ref> As a people, they were [[hunting]] enthusiasts,<ref name="trando" /> tracking down creatures such as [[Frist wolf|frist wolves]]<ref name="THR 2">[[The High Republic (2021) 2|''The High Republic'' (2021) 2]]</ref> and even other sentients.<ref name="PadLost" /> They worshiped a [[Deity|goddess]] called the [[Scorekeeper]].<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> The Trandoshans would also assume control over [[Wasskah]],<ref name="PadLost" /> a [[moon]] of their [[homeworld]].<ref name="VE" /> The Trandoshans shared their star system<ref name="Trandosha location" /> with the planet [[Kashyyyk]], homeworld of the [[Wookiee]]s,<ref name="Ultimate">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> whom the Trandoshans would come to hunt<ref name="Tooth and Claw">{{StoryCite|story=Tooth and Claw|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> and battle in a long-standing, interspecies conflict.<ref name="Yoda 5">[[Yoda 5|''Yoda'' 5]]</ref>

[[File:Garnac2-SWE.png|thumb|right|200px|The Trandoshan Garnac, a big game hunter.]]
The hunter [[Garnac]] had control of the island hunting preserve designated as [[Island Four]] on Wasskah by the time of the [[Clone Wars]]. He ran a [[Garnac's hunting guild|hunting guild]] based out of a [[Ubrikkian Floating Fortress|floating]] [[fortress]] above the island. Garnac's [[scout]]s traveled to different worlds and collect other sentient beings before delivering them to Wasskah and dumping them on Island Four, where the [[prisoner]]s would be hunted for sport. During the [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars, at least three [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi younglings]] had been captured and brought to Wasskah. For a long time, the trio of [[youngling]]s managed to avoid the Trandoshans, who continued to deliver other prey to the island. Eventually, the Trandoshan [[Lo-Taren]] captured the [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] on the planet [[Felucia]] and brought her to island four alongside several other prisoners. Once delivered to the island, Tano escaped and discovered the other younglings.<ref name="PadLost" />

Garnac's [[Reproduction|son]], [[Dar]], later set out to [[Death|kill]] Tano himself as part of an important rite of passage, but was instead killed by the Jedi. Garnac gave chase, killing the youngling [[Kalifa]].<ref name="PadLost" /> Later, other Trandoshan scouts abducted the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]], but before Chewbacca could be successfully delivered, the Trandoshan [[transport]] [[Starship|ship]] was damaged and it crashed on the hunting island. Tano killed the two man crew, and escaped the wreckage with Chewbacca. The Wookiee was able to craft a communications device with some of the scavenged wreckage, and was able to contact the Wookiee [[General]] [[Tarfful]]. Tano, the remaining younglings, and the Wookiee forces [[Battle on Wasskah|engaged]] Garnac's guild on their fortress, and killed all of the Trandoshan hunters.<ref name="WookHunt" /> However, Garnac was the only one to survive the confrontation and ultimately came under the service of the gangster [[Grini Millegi]] on [[Serolonis]].<ref name="Faster">{{TBB|Faster}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the [[bounty hunter]] [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] took on numerous jobs, and eventually acted as a [[bodyguard]] to the upcoming [[bounty]] hunter [[Boba Fett]]. In time, Bossk would be revered as one of the most feared bounty hunters in the [[galaxy]]. On one occasion, Bossk visited the planet [[Lothal]] to collect a bounty on the [[Dug]] criminal [[Gronson Takkaro]]. This brought him into contact with the young [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] youth [[Ezra Bridger]] and into conflict with the corrupt [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Lieutenant]] [[Jenkes]], who was in league with Takkaro. With the help of Bridger, Bossk succeeded in exposing Jenkes' criminal dealings.<ref name="Ezra's Gamble">''[[Ezra's Gamble]]''</ref>

[[File:Noka-2016DoctorAphraAnnual1.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Noka and Kootan]]
During the [[Imperial Era]], five Trandoshans were part of an acquisition crew working for the [[Xonti Brothers]]. Led by [[Noka]], they went to [[Kashyyyk]] to capture Wookiees. [[Kootan]] was keen to kill one but Noka reminded him of the job at hand. Noka used his scanner to locate a Wookiee and they found one which was sleeping. Kootan shot a stun at it to realize it was bleeding and left for dead. The Trandoshans then found themselves under attack by [[Krrsantan]] who killed the other three Trandoshans and pinned down Noka and Kootan. Kootan tried to kill Krrsantan and was knocked out by the Wookiee before being thrown into a tree, killing him. Krrsantan then demanded that Noka brought him to the Xonti Brothers. Noka did so and lived on to tell his story to two journalists.<ref name="Doctor Aphra Annual">[[Doctor Aphra Annual 1|''Doctor Aphra Annual'' 1]]</ref>

[[Feresk Tssat]] served as a member of the [[New Republic]]'s [[Vanguard Squadron]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] following the [[Battle of Endor]], and fought against the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Titan Squadron]].<ref name="Squadrons">''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]''</ref>

==Trandoshans in the galaxy==
[[File:GhaNachkt-MF62.png|thumb|right|250px|Gha Nachkt, a salvage ship captain.]]
{{Quote|Trandoshans are a hardy lot. The preserved jar holds a torn arm from a Trandoshan male, ripped off cleanly by an enraged Wookiee. Analysis with shred skin samples from Bossk's domicile confirmed a match. He's since regenerated that arm. Looks like the old lizard can take more than a punch and return to the fight.|[[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] [[agent]] [[Andressa Divo]]|<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />}}
The [[species]] had a poor history with the Wookiees, who hated the [[Reptile|reptilian]] people.<ref name="Tarfful">{{Databank|tarfful|Tarfful}}</ref> Indeed, the tense [[Separatist Crisis]] period of galactic history saw the port authorities of [[Coruscant Eastern Spaceport]] regularly step into disputes between Trandoshans and Wookiees.<ref name="Coruscant">{{EncyclopediaCite|Coruscant}}</ref> Some Trandoshans found other outlets for work, as opposed to hunting. By the time of the Clone Wars one was [[Gha Nachkt]], who lived life as a salvager. He was eventually hired by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] to scour the sites of damaged ships owned by the [[Galactic Republic]] and find any useful data or scraps. Nachkt eventually recovered the [[R2-series astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]] from a [[Anakin Skywalker's Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Republic Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], but the [[droid]] was eventually [[Raid on Skytop Station|recovered]] by the [[Jedi General]] and [[Jedi Knight|Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], while Nachkt was killed by Confederate General [[Grievous]].<ref name="DotD">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>

Trandoshan Jedi were rare because the culture of their homeworld was the opposite of that of the Jedi. One notable [[Force-sensitive]] Trandoshan was [[Sskeer]], who lived during the [[High Republic Era]].<ref name="Light of the Jedi">''[[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi]]''</ref> Sskeer was a [[Jedi Master]], who was renowned as both a scholar and tactician. His [[Padawan]] was the human [[Keeve Trennis]].<ref name="THR 4">[[The High Republic (2021) 4|''The High Republic'' (2021) 4]]</ref> Sskeer saw action against the [[Nihil]] pirates and carnivorous [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]] sentient plants known as the [[Drengir]].<ref name="THR 1">[[The High Republic (2021) 1|''The High Republic'' (2021) 1]]</ref><ref name="THR 4" /> However, Magrak Syndrome took root in his brain, which limited his connection to the Force<ref name="The High Republic 12" /> but therefore spared him the effects of the [[Shrikarai|Nameless]].<ref name="The High Republic 15">[[The High Republic (2021) 15|''The High Republic'' (2021) 15]]</ref>

[[File:Trandoshan-2024ToppsSWHyperspace.png|thumb|250px|left|Trandoshans often uses weapons suited to their unique physiology.]]
Other Trandoshans during the [[High Republic era]] were the [[Ganguls]] pirate gang leader [[Sellaccc Orryak]] and her nephew [[Daynaal]].<ref name="The Missing Life Day Feast">{{YJA|The Missing Life Day Feast}}</ref> Orryak took over the pirate stronghold [[Yarrum Tower]]<ref name="Tower Run">{{YJA|Tower Run}}</ref> and later attempted to destroy the [[Tenoo Jedi Temple]] during the [[Battle of Tenoo]].<ref name="Battle of Tenoo">{{YJA|The Battle of Tenoo}}</ref> Daynaal, however, rejected his aunt's piratical ways and foiled her plot to sabotage an upcoming [[Life Day]] feast.<ref name="The Missing Life Day Feast" /> The Trandoshan [[Sslanno]], meanwhile, was a [[Nihil]] in [[Pan Eyta's Tempest]] who lost his scales in a plasma blast, which ended up being so damaging those scales never regrew.<ref name="Tempest Runner script" />

The Trandoshan Bossk's bounty hunting career brought him to various locales across the galaxy, and was for a time involved with the bounty hunters [[Aurra Sing]] and [[Castas]]. Bossk and Fett worked with the other bounty hunters in an attempt to avenge Fett's fallen [[Parent|father]], [[Jango Fett|Jango]], by killing [[Mace Windu]], the Jedi who [[First Battle of Geonosis|fought]] and killed Jango. Sing later killed Castas, while Bossk and Fett were arrested by Republic authorities after a failed [[Sabotage of the Endurance|assassination]]. However, during a [[Riot at the Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center|prison riot]], both Bossk and Fett escaped the [[Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center|Republic prison]] they were sent to. They later formed a [[Krayt's Claw|team]] of bounty hunters on the planet [[Tatooine]] and accept a job posted by the [[Belugan]] government on the planet [[Quarzite]]. Although Bossk was subdued by [[Kage Warriors|adversaries]] during the [[Safe cargo objective|mission]], team member [[Asajj Ventress]] was able to complete the mission, to a degree. When Ventress discovered that the cargo they were hired to protect was [[Pluma Sodi]], a [[Homeworld|native]] [[Kage]] [[Gender|female]], Ventress swapped the imprisoned girl with Fett, and was paid for the job's completion before the change was discovered.<ref name="Bounty">{{TCW|Bounty (episode)}}</ref>

[[File:Hunter_Instinct_SWDL.png|thumb|right|250px|Bossk, a well-known bounty hunter during the Clone Wars, and Galactic Civil War]]
[[Nack Movers]] was a Trandoshan [[assassin]] who was well known in the [[Coruscant]] [[Coruscant Underworld|underworld]], and at some point during the Clone Wars he bought a [[Ahsoka Tano's lightsabers|lightsaber]]. He was later murdered by his girlfriend, [[Ione Marcy]], who then took the [[lightsaber]] for herself.<ref name="LL">{{TCW|Lightsaber Lost}}</ref>

[[Ciddarin Scaleback]] was a Trandoshan information broker and cantina owner who owned a [[Cid's Parlor|parlor]] on [[Ord Mantell]]. Following the establishment of the Empire, Scaleback hired the services of a group of rogue [[Clone commando]]s known as [[Clone Force 99|the Bad Batch]]. In return for providing them with shelter and funds, Scaleback hired them as mercenaries for various missions including rescuing the [[rancor]] [[Muchi]],<ref name="Rampage">{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}</ref> recovering the head of a [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|tactical droid]],<ref name="Decommissioned">{{TBB|Decommissioned}}</ref> and the former Separatist [[senator]] [[Avi Singh]]. Scaleback also developed an affectionate relationship with the [[Gender|female]] adolescent clone [[Omega]], helping her hone her potential as a tactician and [[dejarik]] player.<ref name="Common Ground">{{TBB|Common Ground}}</ref> Scaleback and the Bad Batch gradually established a mutually beneficial relationship, with the latter helpiner her to reclaim her parlor from the [[Devaronian]] crime lord [[Roland Durand]].<ref name="Infested">{{TBB|Infested}}</ref>

In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Death year">{{RebelsDate|408}}</ref> Trandoshans [[Seevor]] and [[Proach]] served the [[Mining Guild]] as [[captain]] and [[foreman]] respectively on the [[Ore crawler]], [[Crawler 413-24]], until they were both killed during the [[Hijacking of Crawler 413-24|hijacking]] of the vessel by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] group known as the [[Spectres]].<ref name="Crawler Commandeers">{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}}</ref> In [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Tooth and Claw date note">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|V}} to [[3 ABY]]. The short story "[[Tooth and Claw]]" overlaps with ''The Empire Strikes Back'', thereby placing it in 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] as well.</ref> Bossk encountered his long-presumed dead sister [[Doshanalawook]], who wanted to usher in a new era of Wookiee-Trandoshan cooperation. While he promised to stop hunting Wookies during their meeting,<ref name="Tooth and Claw">{{StoryCite|story=Tooth and Claw|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> Bossk then accepted a job from the [[Galactic Empire]] to find the rebel [[freighter]] known as the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', the crew of which included the Wookiee Chewbacca,<ref name="Empire">{{Film|V}}</ref> whom he was eager to slay.<ref name="Wait for It">{{StoryCite|story=Wait for It|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> He did not complete the job as he was beaten to it by the now adult Boba Fett.<ref name="Empire" />

[[File:DokkStrassi-BoBFCE.png|thumb|left|200px|Dokk Strassi, leader of the Trandoshan family on Tatooine.]]
The [[Strassi family]], crime family of Trandoshans, was part of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt's]] [[Jabba's criminal empire|criminal empire]], with their leader, [[Dokk Strassi]], serving as one of Jabba's captains. Following Jabba's death, in [[4 ABY]], [[Bib Fortuna]],<ref name="Storm">{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}}</ref> the [[Hutt]]'s [[majordomo]],<ref name="Bib Databank">{{Databank|bib-fortuna|Bib Fortuna}}</ref> took over the criminal empire, leading the Trandoshan family to break off and attempt to take his place, to no avail.<ref name="Storm" /> Additionally, the family became protectors of the [[Mos Espa city center|city center]] and business districts of [[Mos Espa]] on Tatooine,<ref name="Stranger">{{BOBF|Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land}}</ref> having an uneasy alliance with Fortuna.<ref name="Streets">{{BOBF|Chapter 3: The Streets of Mos Espa}}</ref>

By [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> during the [[New Republic Era|era]] of the [[New Republic]],<ref name="Chapter 3">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}}</ref> several Trandoshans served within the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] after the [[Battle of Jakku|collapse]] of the Galactic Empire<ref name="Chapter 7">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}}</ref> in [[5 ABY]].<ref name="Jakku Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' establishes that the [[Battle of Jakku]] and therefore the collapse of the [[Galactic Empire]] occurred in 5 ABY.</ref> [[Unidentified Trandoshan bounty hunter|One of these bounty hunters]] accompanied [[Greef Karga]], the leader of the guild, to meet with [[Din Djarin]], a bounty hunter who had gone rogue after [[Clash on Nevarro|rescuing]] a [[Din Grogu|child]] of the same [[species]] as [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]]. After the group set up camp for the night, a group of [[Nevarro reptavian|native reptavians]] attacked them. One of these creatures picked up the Trandoshan with their feet and carried him off into the night.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

[[File:CharrFull-StarWarsHunters.png|thumb|right|250px|Charr armed for battle]]
When Boba Fett, who had retired from bounty hunting, overthrew Bib Fortuna and started his own [[Fett gotra|gotra]] from the late Jabba's empire,<ref name="Storm" /> Strassi of the Trandoshan family paid tribute to the new [[Daimyo]]<ref name="Stranger" /> and agreed to neutrality when the [[Pyke Syndicate]] challenged Fett's territories. In the meantime, some Trandoshan gamblers were attacked by Krrsantan in the [[Sanctuary]] [[cantina]] in Mos Espa. Despite the proprietor [[Garsa Fwip]]'s intervention, Krrsantan ripped the [[Unidentified Trandoshan gambler|one]] of the Trandoshan's arm off.<ref name="Storm" /> When the [[Pyke]]s [[Battle of Mos Espa|attacked]] Mos Espa, the Trandoshan family betrayed Fett and a number of them attacked Krrsantan, who was working for the Daimyo. Krrsantan killed a number of them and escaped, with Fett's assassin [[Fennec Shand]] going on to [[Assassination of the Pyke Syndicate leaders|assassinate]] Strassi.<ref name="Honor">{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}}</ref> Also in 9 ABY,<ref name="Timelines" /> the Trandoshan [[Charr]] was part of the [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]] competition.<ref name="Hunters">''[[Hunters: Battle for the Arena]]''</ref>

A Trandoshan named [[Skreek]] worked for a gang of [[pirate]]s under [[Kragan Gorr]], the [[Warbird gang]], in the late New Republic Era.<ref name="Triple Dark">{{Resistance|The Triple Dark}}</ref> After Gorr allied his gang with the ''[[Colossus]]'' due to their mutual enemy in the [[First Order]],<ref name="No Escape 2">{{Resistance|No Escape: Part 2}}</ref> tensions rose between the pirates and [[Captain]] [[Imanuel Doza]]. In an effort to [[Mutiny on the Colossus|wrestle control of the ''Colossus'']] from Doza, Skreek and his fellow pirates enlisted<ref name="The Mutiny">{{Resistance|The Mutiny}}</ref> a [[B1's B2-series super battle droid battalion|battalion]]<ref name="B1">{{Databank|b1|B1}}</ref> of [[B2-series super battle droid]]s from pirate [[Sidon Ithano]], only for the reprogrammed [[B1-series battle droid]] "[[B1 (Colossus)|B1]]" to take control of the force. Skreek and his fellow pirates were then exiled from the ''Colossus''.<ref name="The Mutiny" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Trandoshan species first appeared in the [[1980]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] in the form of a cameo appearance by the bounty hunter Bossk. The Trandoshans also appeared in numerous [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] products including the [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] [[Marvel Comics]], the [[Star Wars: Young Jedi Knights|''Young Jedi Knights'']] young adult novel series, and [[Dark Horse Comics]]' [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Knights of the Old Republic'']] comics. The species have also appeared in several [[Canon]] products including the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', [[Ryder Windham]]'s young reader novella ''[[Ezra's Gamble]]'', and the Marvel comic series [[Star Wars: Darth Vader (2015)|''Star Wars Darth Vader'']].

Trandoshans have also appeared as the secondary antagonists of the non-Canon ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures]]'' episode "[[Peril on Kashyyyk]]," which premiered on [[Disney XD]] on [[June 27]], [[2016]]. In this story, the Trandoshans and Wookiees are depicted as having an antagonistic relationship with the former acting as proxies for the Galactic Empire. The Trandoshans take [[Chief]] [[Attiburra]]'s son [[Tantarra]] and hold him hostage in an island fortress. The [[Freemakers/LEGO|Freemakers]], a [[Scavenger|scavenging]] family, rescue him in return for obtaining a piece of [[wroshyr wood]] from the Wookiees.
